# py-kit Plugin Developer Guide

py-kit is a plugin that provides Python implementation conventions and scaffold generation.
**The overall policy was completely overhauled in v2.0.0 (PR138 / PR140).** It moved from the old v1 (pure DDD base) to v2 (feature-folder layout + function-first + TypeScript-style).

---

## Overall Policy (v2.0.0)

| | Adopted | Discontinued |
|---|---|---|
| Layout | Feature-folder layout (`src/{pkg}/{shared,features,integrations,runtime,server}/`) | Pure DDD (`domain` / `application` / `infrastructure` / `interface`) |
| Design | Function-first (DTO + module functions) + DI via function type aliases | Class-based DI, Repository classes, Provider classes |
| Types | Python 3.12+ / PEP 695 `type` statement / `Protocol` / `Callable` | `TypeAlias` compatibility / Java-style interface inheritance |
| DB | Out of scope (Web is delegated to next-kit) | Repository pattern |
| Testing | Integration tests + smoke tests only. No unit tests | Unit tests at all layers |
| Comments | One-line docstring required for exported items, description required for design-critical fields (consistent with next-kit) | docstring optional |

See `references/index.yaml` (reference list), `references/injection_rules.yaml` (injection rules), and each reference body for details.

---

## Structure of references

```
references/
├── CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.jp.md  # Minimal role description for the two management files
├── index.yaml                  # Reference list + one-line description (English; parsed by hook)
├── index.jp.yaml               # JP mirror of index.yaml (human-only)
├── injection_rules.yaml      # Edit-path pattern → required/optional references (language-independent)
├── core/                     # Language rules (naming, comments, types, style, decorators)
├── architecture/             # Feature-folder layout + function wiring + dependency direction + principles + refactor judgement
├── shared/                   # logger / settings / secrets-and-env / errors / types / constants
├── scripts/                  # Single-file scripts + launcher + tkinter
├── testing/                  # Integration tests + smoke policy + Mock patterns
├── concurrency/              # asyncio + parallelism
├── packaging/                # pyproject.toml + uv + distribution
├── performance/              # Profiler cheat sheet
├── llm/                      # LLM providers / Instructor / prompts authoring + loader / caching
└── fastapi/                  # app / routes / schemas / auth-errors / health
```

39 reference files in total (78 including JP mirrors).

---

## Role separation: index.yaml vs injection_rules.yaml

| File | Contents | Language |
|---|---|---|
| `index.yaml` | All references' `path` + one-line `description` as a YAML list | English (parsed by the hook) |
| `index.jp.yaml` | JP mirror (for humans browsing) | Japanese |
| `injection_rules.yaml` | Star chart mapping edit-target file-path patterns to `required` / `optional` references | Language-independent |

The `py-kit-references-injection` hook (PreToolUse) reads these on every `Edit` / `Write` / `MultiEdit` / `Read` and auto-injects matched references into Claude's context via `decision: block`.

---

## Skills

| Skill | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `py-kit:py-project` | General Python projects (new / existing). Scaffold generation in the feature-folder layout, or review / extension of existing code |
| `py-kit:py-script` | Simple scripts of a single file or a few files |

No skill-selection hook. Skills are invoked **explicitly** by the user (`/py-kit:py-project`, `/py-kit:py-script`). Auto-dispatching was removed in PR140 — the references auto-injection hook (`inject_references.py`) already delivers the relevant references on every `Edit` / `Write`, so a separate dispatch hook is redundant.

---

## Hook Design Policy

py-kit hooks follow the `claude-kit` policy:
- File-type guards are `PreToolUse` (not `UserPromptSubmit`)
- Session-flag-style blocking (`/tmp/{hook-name}-{session_id}`) — block only once per session
- Do not add dispatch-purpose `UserPromptSubmit` hooks

The **references auto-injection hook** (`py-kit-references-injection`) was migrated to the
`ref-inject` mechanism in v2.4.0 (PR157). Regenerate it via `/ref-inject:apply`, never hand-edit
`hooks/inject_references.py` per plugin. It follows this policy:
- On `PreToolUse(Edit|Write|MultiEdit|Read)`, read `references/injection_rules.yaml` and look up descriptions in `references/index.yaml`
- Match the file path against `rules[].pattern` (glob)
- Inject matched `required` as **full body**, `optional` as **path + description only**, via the Jinja2 template into `decision: block` reason
- Claude reads `optional` reference bodies itself via `Read` as needed
- Read fires so that issue-scan and other read paths also receive reference guidance
- A **two-tier TTL token** (`~/.claude/tokens/py-kit/{session_id}.yaml`) de-dupes injection: a YAML map with `patterns` and `references` namespaces, each entry carrying `expires_at` (epoch seconds, = injection time + TTL). The `patterns` tier skips an already-injected pattern while `now < expires_at`; the `references` tier shows a `required` reference already injected this session (via any pattern) by **path only** — so a reference bound to multiple patterns is never re-injected as full body. Both re-inject once `now >= expires_at`
- TTL defaults to **3600s**, overridable via `settings.json` `env` `PY_KIT_INJECTION_TTL` (seconds, shared by both tiers). Every fire scans all session tokens, drops expired entries from both namespaces, and deletes emptied token files
- **No `PreCompact` hook** — after `/compact` the bodies re-inject once the TTL elapses; a dedicated compact-refresh hook was judged unnecessary (decided in PR156)

## Versions

| Version | Main change |
|---|---|
| 2.5.0 | Injection token is now **two-tier** (`patterns` + `references` namespaces). A `required` reference shared across multiple patterns is injected full body only once per session; subsequent patterns show it by path only (regenerated from ref-inject templates; PR160) |
| 2.4.0 | Migrated the injection hook to the `ref-inject` mechanism (regenerate via `/ref-inject:apply`). `required` references are injected **full body** again, `optional` as path + description; per-pattern **TTL token** (`{session_id}.yaml` map with `expires_at`, default 3600s, env `PY_KIT_INJECTION_TTL`) replaces the empty marker files; no `PreCompact` hook (PR157) |
| 2.3.1 | Removed the optional `session-kit` companion (deleted as a plugin). Injection tokens now always live for the whole session (once-per-pattern); doc/comment cleanup only, no code-behavior change (PR155) |
| 2.3.0 | `core/comments.md`: comment the content of multi-step functions, not just block markers — per-step intent + per-branch labels, applied regardless of layer; "no comments on logging-only lines"; worked example (PR154) |
| 2.2.0 | Injection token is now per-pattern (was per-file); session-kit (optional) resets tokens per turn via UserPromptSubmit. Drops the PR150 marker/mtime approach (PR151) |
| 2.1.2 | Injection token honors session-kit's context-generation marker → re-inject after /compact and /clear (PR150) |
| 2.1.1 | Injection hook: inject path+description only (no body) as absolute paths; Read matcher kept (PR147) |
| 2.0.0 | Complete overhaul to feature-folder layout + function-first + TypeScript-style (policy fixed in PR138, implemented in PR140) |
| 1.0.0 | Pure DDD base (discontinued) |

See `changelogs/v{version}.md` for details.
